messages:
Ben: Heads-up — ACME hit support asking for temporary unredact access to one tenant's request traces for a PCI incident. need a safe flow.
Cara: Are they asking to see full request bodies or just headers/ids?
Ben: full request/responses for a handful of request_ids. they're on Dedicated and have an SLA for debug assistance.
Diego: We can't just flip unredact globally. privacy policy + audit trail required.
Alice: Agree. We should provide a time-limited, scoped token that lets ops view redacted fields unmasked for specific request_ids. call it `grace-viewer`?
Eve: Product + legal both approved a controlled inspector mode, but UX needs guardrails so engineers don't overuse it.
Marta: Key constraints: 1) tenant consent recorded, 2) immutable audit log of who viewed what, 3) TTL <= 24h, 4) sampling not bypassed — only requested items.
Ben: Proposed flow: support creates a ticket -> ops generates grace-viewer token scoped to tenant + request_ids -> token recorded in audit -> token auto-revoked at TTL.
Cara: How do we prevent tokens from being used to sweep other tenant data? must be tenant-scoped and route-checked.
Diego: Enforce at routing layer: token includes tenant_id and request_ids hash; the proxy verifies both before unmasking.
Alice: UX: Console should show a one-click "Request Unmask" that pre-fills tenant and request ids from ticket. Button triggers an internal workflow and creates the token.
Eve: For auditability, show who requested, approver, TTL, purpose string. Prevent reuse of the same token across tickets.
Ben: Quotas — we should gate number of unmask requests per tenant per month. Do we enforce at API gateway or via policy service?
Cara: Policy service (rbac + quota) is better. It already tracks per-tenant quotas for debug endpoints.
Marta: Important: sampling. If telemetry sampling removed PII before storage (eg pre-scrub step), we can't reconstruct. Need a prerequisite check: trace must be stored un-scrubbed under tenant's encrypted bucket. If not, return a denial.
Diego: Add a validation step in the flow: service checks storage policy for those request_ids and responds with allowed/denied reason codes.
Alice: Edge case: overlapping request_ids from multiple tenants (rare). We should always validate tenant ownership before unmask.
Ben: Implementation notes: new API endpoint POST /internal/unmask-tokens {tenant_id, request_ids[], ttl_seconds, reason} returns token and audit_id.
Cara: Example token creation curl for ops:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_KEY" -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/v1/unmask-tokens \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"acme", "request_ids":["r:123","r:124"], "ttl_seconds":3600, "reason":"PCI support"}'
```
Alice: The token format should be short-lived JWT signed by KMS with custom claims: tenant, request_hashes, iat, exp, audit_id.
Marta: Audit must include: requester_id, approver_id (if we require approval), request_ids, TTL, justification, and IP.
Eve: Approvals — do we want manual approval for all requests or auto-approve for high-tier customers? product says high-tier auto, others manual with 1-hour SLA.
Diego: From privacy POV, tiered auto-approval is OK if we log and send alerts to compliance team for every auto-grant.
Ben: Routing: when proxy sees Authorization: Bearer <grace-token>, it calls policy service to validate signature and claims and returns an allow-unmask flag per request_id.
Cara: Performance: validating per request_id can add latency. We should batch-check claims once per token use and cache the result for the token's TTL.
Alice: Also need console UX for replaying masked->unmasked side-by-side and a clear banner that explains this is privileged data and will be audited.
Eve: Add ephemeral watermark on exported artifacts (PDF/CSV) that include unmasked data: "Exported by <name> for <reason> at <time>".
Marta: Exports should be blocked unless explicit export permission granted in token claims.
Ben: Telemetry: we must instrument metrics: unmask_requests_total, unmask_denied_reasons, avg-token-lifetime, per-tenant-unmask_count. wire to alert if sudden spike.
Cara: Also an audit-only stream to S3 with higher retention for compliance (30-90d depending on region/legal). We should keep hashed copies of tokens to detect reuse attempts.
Diego: Security: rotate the signing key monthly; tokens issued before rotation must still validate until expiry — so keep previous keys for validation window.
Alice: Rollout plan: feature flag gated; start internal-only, then dedicated customer beta, then general release. Add canary for console button exposure.
Ben: Who picks up infra pieces? I'll take the proxy validation + token endpoint. Cara you want the policy service quota + caching? Alice do console changes.
Cara: I'll take policy + quota caching + metrics. estimate 3 sprint-ish including tests.
Alice: I'll do the console flow and export watermark. need mockups, I'll ping design.
Diego: I'll own the privacy checklist and approve final audit schema.
Marta: I'll draft the legal blurb for support consent and retention timelines.
Eve: I'll coordinate beta customers and product notes. also add the billing/usage implications to pricing team.
InfraBot: Deployment note: create feature flag `unmask.grace_viewer` scoped to env and tenant. Canary to `eng-test` first.
Ben: Ok let's sync tomorrow 11am to map tickets. For now I'll write the API sketch and link PR when ready.
Cara: thx — filed ENG-9876 for policy work.
Alice: filed WEB-4721 for console.
Diego: Privacy checklist id: PRIV-128.
Marta: Legal ticket LEG-332 created.
Eve: I'll invite ACME to beta once infra is up.
Ben: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Cara: :eyes:
Diego: will review the API draft today.
Alice: mockups by EOD.
InfraBot: Reminder: run canary smoke after deploy — /run-smoke eng-test unmask-flow
Ben: closing thread, followups in the tickets.
